title: The reasoning-model link: does a deception probe read the CoT or the hidden computation?

original_idea.body: On an open reasoning model, construct hidden-objective cases with innocuous CoT and test whether a deception probe fires despite clean CoT; AUROC conditioned on clean CoT.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: detecting hidden goals despite clean CoT addresses a flagged CoT-unfaithfulness threat (level 4).

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Constructing reliable clean-CoT hidden-goal cases and verifying CoT-independence needs solid judgment (level 3).

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but model-organism setup adds dependency (level 4).

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Hidden-goal/CoT-faithfulness monitoring is a neglected high-counterfactual model-organism slice (level 5).

low_compute.reasoning: Reasoning-model inference + probe; single GPU, mid-range.

novelty.reasoning: Probing hidden goals conditioned on clean CoT is a fresh decomposition; mostly novel.
